discovery: Discovery of high-energy astrophysical neutrinos and the opening of neutrino astronomy with the IceCube Neutrino Observatory
motivation: Francis Halzen conceived and led IceCube, which turned a cubic kilometre of Antarctic ice into a neutrino telescope, growing out of the AMANDA pioneer effort. In 2013 IceCube reported a diffuse flux of high-energy neutrinos of extraterrestrial origin. The claim has held up through years of independent analyses and channels: starting events, through-going muons, and the Glashow resonance event. Since then IceCube has linked neutrinos to the blazar TXS 0506+056 in a multimessenger campaign. It has found evidence for neutrino emission from the Seyfert galaxy NGC 1068 and observed the Galactic plane in neutrinos. These results come from careful statistical treatment of large backgrounds, with blind analyses and pre-defined significance thresholds. They opened a genuinely new observational window on the high-energy universe, the first since gravitational waves, and fulfilled a decades-old vision of particle astrophysics. This instrument-driven discovery merits the Nobel Prize.
